message.content:
**Kings of France in the 18th Century**

| King | Reign |
|------|-------|
| **Louis XV** – “the Beloved” | 21 September 1715 – 10 May 1774 |
| **Louis XVI** – “the Last Bourbon Monarch” | 20 August 1774 – 21 January 1792 |

> *After Louis XV’s death, the throne passed to his great‑grandson Louis XVI.*  
> 
> In 1792 the French Revolution deposed the monarchy; it would not return until the Restoration in 1814 (with Louis XVIII). Thus, within the calendar years 1701‑1800, the only reigning sovereigns of France were Louis XV and Louis XVI.
message.reasoning:
We need to answer who were the kings of France during the 18th century (1701-1800). The user asks "who were the kings". We can provide names with reign periods.

The question likely expects listing Louis XV (1715–1774), Louis XVI (1774–1792) until monarchy abolished; also mention Louis XVIII after restoration but that's early 19th century. Also maybe include earlier part of 18th century had no king before 1715 because regency under Philippe II d'Orléans from 1723? Actually Louis XIV died 1715, his son Louis XV ascended at age five. So we should list:

Louis XV (r. 1715–1774)
Louis XVI (r. 1774–1792)

Also note that there was a period of regency between 1715-1723 when Duke of Orléan served as Regent. But not a king. After 1792 monarchy ended due to revolution. Then later restored monarchy under Louis XVII (though he never reigned, died child). And then Louis XVIII (1814-1830).
